Rashi on Pesachim 73a:10:1.hebrew: אשם שניתק לרעיה - שמתו בעליו או נתכפרו באחר, וחטאת ואשם אינן באין נדבה, ומשנתכפרו באחר אין תקנה לזה. וגבי חטאת הילכתא גמירי לה (תמורה כא:) דמתה, ובאשם גמירי הילכתא (שם יח.) כל שבחטאת מתה באשם רועה. ואם ניתקו מעליו והשליכו לאפר לרעות שיסתאב ויפול בו מום, שיוכל לפדותו ולהוציאו לחולין — וכל הרועים דמיהם נופלים לנדבה. ומה היא נדבה? ששה שופרות היו במקדש וכתוב עליהן "נדבה", ושם היו נותנין כל מותר דמי חטאת ואשם, ומביאין משם קיץ המזבח, עולות: בשר לשם ועורות לכהנים, שזהו מדרשו של יהוידע הכהן במס' תמורה (דף כג:). וזה לא המתין עד שיומם, ומשניתקו לרעייה שחטו סתם — כשר לעולת קיץ המזבח, הואיל וסוף סוף דמיו לכך היו עומדים:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:10:1.english: A guilt-offering that was consigned to grazing - [Where] its owners died or achieved atonement through another [guilt-offering], and a sin-offering and a guilt-offering cannot be brought as a freewill-offering, so once they achieved atonement through another, there is no remedy for this [animal]. Regarding a sin-offering, a traditional law was learned (Temurah 21b) that it is left to die, whereas regarding a guilt-offering, a traditional law was learned (ibid. 18a): Whatever [case] in a sin-offering is left to die, in a guilt-offering it grazes. And if he removed it from himself and cast it to the meadow to graze so that it will become disqualified and a blemish will befall it, so that he can redeem it and release it to non-sacred status — for all [animals] that graze, their proceeds fall to freewill-offering. And what is "freewill-offering"? There were six horn-shaped chests in the Temple, and "Freewill-offering" was written on them, and there they would place all surplus proceeds of sin-offerings and guilt-offerings, and from there they would bring "summer-fruit of the altar," burnt-offerings: the meat for God and the hides for the priests, for this is the exposition of Jehoiada the Priest in Tractate Temurah (23b). Now this person did not wait until it became blemished, and once he consigned it to grazing, he slaughtered it without specifying [its purpose] — it is valid as a burnt-offering for the summer-fruit of the altar, since ultimately its proceeds were destined for this.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:10:2.hebrew: לא בעי עקירה - מאחר שהוא עומד לכך, א"צ לעקור שם אשם ממנו:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:10:2.english: It does not require uprooting - Since it stands for this [purpose], there is no need to uproot the designation of guilt-offering from it.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:11:1.hebrew: א"ה כי לא ניתק נמי - משעה שנתכפר באחר, סתמיה לקיץ המזבח קאי:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:11:1.english: If so, even when it has not been consigned [to grazing] - From the moment [the owner] achieved atonement through another [offering], by default it stands [designated] for supplementary burnt-offerings of the altar.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:11:2.hebrew: גזירה לאחר כפרה אטו קודם שנתכפר - דסתמיה לאשם, אבל משניתק לא מיחלף:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:11:2.english: A decree [for] after atonement due to before [the owner] achieved atonement - For its default [status] is as a guilt-offering, but once it has been consigned [to grazing], it will not be confused [with one before atonement].

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:12:1.hebrew: ומנא תימרא - להא מילתא דאמר לך דגזרי' הכי:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:12:1.english: And from where do you say - [regarding] this matter that [the Gemara] said to you, that we decree thus.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:12:2.english: For a free-will offering - For the shofar-shaped [collection] chests.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:12:3.hebrew: ר' אליעזר אומר ימות - כל צדדיו של רבי אליעזר, היה עושה אשם כחטאת לכל דבר, שנאמר (ויקרא ז׳:ז׳) כחטאת כאשם; וכן גבי שלא לשמו, וכן גבי חטאת שנכנס דמה לפנים במס' זבחים (דף יוד:):
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:12:3.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: It dies - [In] all his positions, Rabbi Eliezer treated a guilt-offering like a sin-offering in every respect, as it is stated (Leviticus 7:7): "As the sin-offering, so is the guilt-offering"; and similarly regarding [a sacrifice slaughtered] not for its own sake, and similarly regarding a sin-offering whose blood entered the inner [sanctuary], in Tractate Zevachim (10b).

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:12:4.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: It is sold - After it becomes blemished.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:12:5.hebrew: ויביא בדמיו עולה - נדבה לעצמו. ובמס' תמורה מסיק להא מילתא: והלא אף הנדבה עולה היא, מה בין דברי רבי יהושע לדברי חכמים? אלא שבזמן שהיא באה לחובתו, הוא סומך עליה ושוחטה ונסכיה קריבין משלו; וכשהיא באה לנדבת ציבור, אינו סומך עליה כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:12:5.english: And he brings a burnt-offering with its money - A free-will offering for himself. And in Tractate Temurah [the Gemara] concludes this matter: Is not the [communal] free-will offering also a burnt-offering? What is [the difference] between the words of Rabbi Yehoshua and the words of the Sages? Rather, when it comes for his [personal] obligation, he lays [his] hands on it and slaughters it, and its libations are offered from his [own funds]; whereas when it comes as a communal free-will offering, he does not lay [his] hands on it, etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:13:1.hebrew: בדמיו אין - אבל איהו גופיה לא אמר דיקרב עולה, ואף על פי שמקריבו לעצמו. אלמא גזירה לאחר כפרה, שנתכפר באחר, אטו לפני כפרה. דאי שרית ליה השתא, טעי, ואי מיצטריך ליה עולה נמי קודם כפרה, מקריב ליה להאי והדר מייתי אחר לאשם, ואי אפשר לשנות זבח לזבח אחר כ"ז שעומד לשמו:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:13:1.english: With its money, yes - But [regarding] the [animal] itself, he did not say that it should be offered as a burnt-offering, even though he offers it for himself. Evidently, [it is] a decree [applying] after atonement — when he has achieved atonement with another [animal] — on account of [the case] before atonement. For if you permit it to him now, he will err, and when he also needs a burnt-offering before atonement, he will offer this [animal as a burnt-offering] and then bring another for a guilt-offering; yet it is impossible to change a sacrifice into another sacrifice as long as it stands in its [original] designation.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:1:1.english: A service of gift - The priestly gifts that I have given you, behold, they are like [Temple] service.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:2:1.english: It is obvious. Since there - In [the chapter] Tamid Nishchat (daf 61a), we learned [in a Mishnah] that a Paschal offering [slaughtered] for those who cannot eat it is invalid.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:2:2.hebrew: הכא - דבשבת קאי, ממילא שמעינן דחייב:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:2:2.english: Here - Which refers to Shabbat; we automatically infer that he is liable.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:2:3.hebrew: משום דבעי למיתנא סיפא "לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו פטור", תנא רישא "שלא לאוכליו חייב":
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:2:3.english: Because [the Tanna] wanted to teach in the latter clause, "For those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it, [he is] exempt," he taught in the first clause, "For those who cannot eat it, [he is] liable."

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:4:1.hebrew: לדברי האומר - במס' שבת (דף קו.):
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:4:1.english: According to the one who says - In Tractate Shabbat (106a).

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:4:2.hebrew: מקלקל בחבורה - העושה חבורה בשבת לקלקלה, שאינו מתקן, פטור. ואין חובל חייב משום שבת, אלא שוחט שמתקן, או חובל בבהמה וצריך לדם להאכילו לכלבו:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:4:2.english: One who inflicts a destructive wound - One who inflicts a wound on Shabbat to ruin [it], such that he does not improve [anything], is exempt. And one who inflicts a wound is not liable on account of Shabbat unless [he is] one who slaughters, who improves [it], or one who wounds an animal and needs the blood to feed it to his dog.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:4:3.hebrew: שלא לאוכליו חייב - דקתני מתני' חייב:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:4:3.english: For those who cannot eat it, [he is] liable - For the Mishnah teaches, "[He is] liable."

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:4:4.english: What has he improved - Behold, he has disqualified it.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:5:1.hebrew: תיקן - דכל הקרבנות שנפסלו בעזרה, תנן במס' זבחים (דף פד.), אם עלו למזבח אימוריהן להקטיר, לא ירדו:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:5:1.english: He has improved [it] - For [regarding] all offerings that were disqualified in the [Temple] courtyard, we learned in Tractate Zevachim (84a) [that] if their sacrificial parts ascended to the altar to be burned, they do not descend.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:5:2.hebrew: בעלי מומין - תנן התם: אם עלו ירדו, שלא היה פסולן בקודש:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:5:2.english: Blemished [offerings] - We learned there: If they ascended [the altar], they must descend, because their disqualification was not in the Sanctuary.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:6:1.hebrew: בדוקין שבעין - טליי"א, כגון "הנוטה כדוק שמים" (ישעיהו מ׳:כ״ב). וגבי קרבן מום הוא, כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״א:כ׳) "או דק או תבלול בעינו":
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:6:1.english: With a film [cataract] in the eye - [In Old French,] taie [a film or web on the eye], like [the verse] "Who stretches out the heavens like a curtain [dok]" (Isaiah 40:22). And with regard to a sacrifice, it is a blemish, as it is written (Leviticus 21:20): "or a cataract [dak], or a commingling in his eye."

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:6:2.hebrew: ואליבא דר"ע - במס' זבחים תנן: ר"ע מכשיר בבעלי מומין אם עלו, ואמרו בגמרא: לא ארע"ק אלא בדוקין שבעין, הואיל וכשירין לכתחלה בעופות:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:6:2.english: And in accordance with Rabbi Akiva - In Tractate Zevachim we learned [in a Mishnah]: Rabbi Akiva declares blemished [offerings] valid if they ascended [the altar], and they said in the Gemara: Rabbi Akiva stated [this] only regarding cataracts in the eye, since they are valid ab initio in bird [offerings].

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:7:1.hebrew: טריפה - אמר התם, אם עלתה תרד:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:7:1.english: Tereifa - [It] says there: If it went up [onto the altar], it must come down.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:7:2.english: From [the status of] a carcass - From imparting ritual impurity.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:8:1.hebrew: השוחט חטאת - גר', ובשחיטת חולין בפרק שני מפרש אמאי נקט חטאת:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:8:1.english: One who slaughters a sin-offering - This is the reading, and in [Tractate] Shechitat Chullin in the second chapter it explains why [the baraita] specified a sin-offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:8:2.hebrew: ג' חטאות - משום שבת, ומשום ע"ז, ומשום שחוטי חוץ לעזרה:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:8:2.english: Three sin-offerings - Because of Shabbat, and because of idolatry, and because of [offerings] slaughtered outside the [Temple] courtyard.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:8:3.hebrew: מה תיקן - הכא אפי' לטהרו מידי נבילה ליכא, דתקרובת ע"ז מטמאה אפי' באהל:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:8:3.english: What has he improved - Here, there is not even [the benefit of] purifying it from [the impurity of] a carcass, for an idolatrous offering imparts impurity even in a tent.

Rashi on Pesachim 73a:9:1.hebrew: מידי אבר מן החי - לבני נח, שאם אכלו אינו נהרג:
Rashi on Pesachim 73a:9:1.english: Out of [the category of] a limb from a living creature - For Noahides, for if he eats it, he is not executed.

Tosafot on Pesachim 73a:10:1.hebrew: אשם שניתק לרעיה ושחטו סתם כשר - כל עיקר רעיה מדרבנן, דמדאורייתא לא צריך רעיה כלל, ולהכי קאמר: "אלמא לא בעי עקירה". "א"ה, כי לא ניתק נמי" — אי אמרת בשלמא בעי עקירה, א"ש דבעינן ניתק, דע"י ניתק יזכור לעוקרו, אבל לא ניתק לא, דגזרי' עוקרו אטו לא עוקרו; אבל השתא דלא בעי עקירה, קודם ניתוק נמי ליכשר, דליכא למיחש למידי. ומשני: דקודם ניתוק גזרי' אחר כפרה אטו לפני כפרה, ואחר ניתוק נמי דיעבד כשר, אבל לכתחלה מיהא גזרי' אטו לפני כפרה. ומנא תימרא? דתנן "אשם כו'", "בדמיו אין, אבל הוא גופיה לא" — דהא כ"ע מודו דלאחר עקירה וניתוק היה יכול לשוחטו לכתחלה, דליכא למיגזר אטו קודם עקירה הואיל ואיכא היכירא דניתוק, אי לאו משום דגזרינן לאחר כפרה וניתוק אטו קודם כפרה. ומה שפי' ר"י, דאי אמרת דבעי עקירה אתי שפיר דגזרו בשלא ניתק דילמא אתי לשחוט בלא עקירה — ק': א"כ, פסח בשאר ימות השנה דבעי עקירה, אמאי לא מצריך רעיה? מקשי': דאמר פ"ק דמנחות (דף ד.): "א"ר הונא אמר רב: אשם שניתק לרעיה ושחטו סתם — כשר לעולה. ניתק — אין, לא ניתק — לא. מ"ט? אמר קרא 'הוא', בהוייתו יהא". אלמא ניתוק דאורייתא הוא, והכא משמע שהוא מדרבנן וגזרי' אטו קודם כפרה! ואור"י דה"פ: התם אמר קרא "הוא" — בהוייתו יהא קודם כפרה; וכיון דמדאורייתא הוי בהוייתו קודם כפרה, גזרי' אחר כפרה אטו קודם כפרה. ור"ת פי' דה"ק במנחות: "ניתק — אין, לא ניתק — לא", וטעמא כדמפרש הכא, דגזרי' אטו לפני כפרה. ומסיק: "מ"ט? אמר קרא 'הוא'", כלומר: מ"ט כשר? הלא הלכה למשה מסיני הוא דכל שבחטאת מתה, באשם רועה! אמר קרא "הוא", משמע בהוייתו שלבסוף, כשיסתאב וימכר שהדמים לנדבה, והויא עולה; ואתא קרא ללמוד על הלכה, דהכי גמרינן דכל שבחטאת מתה באשם קרב עולה; א"נ כי גמרי' דבאשם רועה — למצוה; א"נ דבאשם אזיל לנדבת ציבור, ולא ידעי' אי הוא עצמו או דמיו, וגלי קרא דהוא עצמו. ואי לאו הלכה, ה"א "הוא" בהוייתו דמעיקרא יהא, ולא יקרב עולה. וראי' לפי' זה, דבתמורה פ' אלו קדשים (תמורה דף יח.) גר' בכל הספרים: "א"ר הונא: אשם שניתק לרעיה ושחטו סתם — כשר. מ"ט? אמר קרא 'הוא', בהוייתו יהא", ולא גר' התם בשום ספר "ניתק — אין, לא ניתק — לא":
Tosafot on Pesachim 73a:10:1.english: A guilt-offering that was consigned to grazing and he slaughtered it without specifying [its purpose] is valid [as a burnt-offering] - The entire requirement of grazing is rabbinic, for by Torah law it does not require grazing at all, and therefore [the Gemara] says: "Apparently it does not require uprooting." "If so, when it has not been consigned [to grazing], also!" — granted, if you say it requires uprooting, it works out well that we require it to be consigned [to grazing], for through being consigned [to grazing] one will remember to uproot it, whereas [when it has] not [been] consigned, no, for we decree [concerning] one who uproots it on account of one who does not uproot it; but now that it does not require uprooting, before being consigned [to grazing] it should also be valid, since there is nothing to be concerned about! And [the Gemara] answers that before being consigned [to grazing] we decree [concerning] after atonement on account of before atonement; and even after being consigned [to grazing] it is valid after the fact, whereas initially we still decree on account of before atonement. And from where do you say [this]? As we learned [in the Mishnah]: "A guilt-offering etc."; "with its money, yes, but [the animal] itself, no" — for everyone agrees that after uprooting and being consigned [to grazing] one would be able to slaughter it initially, since there would be no [reason] to decree on account of before uprooting, inasmuch as there is the distinguishing sign of being consigned [to grazing], were it not for the fact that we decree [concerning] after atonement and being consigned [to grazing] on account of before atonement. And regarding what the Ri explained — that if you say it requires uprooting, it works out well that they decreed when it was not consigned [to grazing] lest one come to slaughter without uprooting — it is difficult: if so, a Paschal lamb during the rest of the days of the year, which requires uprooting, why does it not require grazing? [Moreover,] we raise an objection: for it is stated in the first chapter of Menachot (4a): "Rav Huna said in the name of Rav: A guilt-offering that was consigned to grazing and he slaughtered it without specifying [its purpose] is valid as a burnt-offering; if it was consigned [to grazing], yes; if it was not consigned [to grazing], no. What is the reason? The verse says 'it is' — it shall remain in its [original] state." Apparently, being consigned [to grazing] is by Torah law, whereas here it is implied that it is rabbinic and we decree on account of before atonement! And the Ri says that this is what it means: there, the verse says "it is" — it shall remain in its [original] state before atonement; and since by Torah law it remains in its [original] state before atonement, we decree [concerning] after atonement on account of before atonement. And Rabbeinu Tam explained that this is what [the Gemara] is saying in Menachot: "if it was consigned [to grazing], yes; if it was not consigned [to grazing], no" — and the reason is as [the Gemara] explains here, that we decree on account of before atonement. And it concludes: "What is the reason? The verse says 'it is'" — that is to say, what is the reason it is valid? Is it not a law [transmitted] to Moses from Sinai that whatever in a sin-offering is left to die, in a guilt-offering grazes? The verse says "it is," which implies in its ultimate state, when it becomes blemished and is sold so that the money goes for a free-will offering, and it becomes a burnt-offering; and the verse comes to teach regarding the [oral] law, that we learn that whatever in a sin-offering is left to die, in a guilt-offering is offered as a burnt-offering. Alternatively, when we learn that in a guilt-offering it grazes, [that is] for the preferred mitzvah. Alternatively, [we learned] that in a guilt-offering it goes for a communal free-will offering, and we would not know whether [it is] the animal itself or its monetary value, so the verse reveals that [it is] the animal itself; and were it not for the [oral] law, I would have said "it is" means it shall remain in its original state and not be offered as a burnt-offering. And a proof for this explanation is that in Temurah, in the chapter Eilu Kodashim (Temurah 18a), it is read in all the texts: "Rav Huna said: A guilt-offering that was consigned to grazing and he slaughtered it without specifying [its purpose] is valid. What is the reason? The verse says 'it is' — it shall remain in its [original] state," and it does not read there in any text "if it was consigned [to grazing], yes; if it was not consigned [to grazing], no."

Tosafot on Pesachim 73a:4:1.hebrew: לדברי האומר מקלקל בחבורה כו' - וא"ת: והלא ר' יהודה הוא דפטר מקלקל בחבורה, ומתני' דמחייב בשאינן ראויין — דהיינו מתעסק, ששוחט זבח זה וסבור שהוא אחר — לא אתי כר"י, דלדידיה מתעסק פטור, כדמוכח בפ' ספק אכל (כריתות יט:), דקאמר: "הנח לתינוקות, מתוך שמקלקל בחבורה חייב, מתעסק נמי חייב", אלמא משמע: מאן דפטר מקלקל בחבורה פטר נמי מתעסק, וא"כ מתני' לא מתוקמא כמאן דפטר מקלקל בחבורה! וי"ל, ד"לדברי האומר מקלקל בחבורה פטור" היינו רבי יוחנן אליבא דרבי שמעון, דפטר היכא דמקלקל לגמרי, דליכא תיקון כלל, ולאפוקי מדר' אבהו; דבפ' האורג (שבת קו.) תני ר' אבהו קמיה דר' יוחנן: "כל המקלקלין פטורין חוץ מחובל ומבעיר". א"ל: "פוק תני לברא, 'חובל ומבעיר' אינה משנה! ואת"ל משנה — בחובל וצריך לכלבו, ומבעיר וצריך לאפרו". והיינו אליבא דר"ש, מדמפליג בין חובל ומבעיר לשאר מקלקלין, אבל מקלקל גמור לא, אפי' לר"ש. מיהו אכתי קשה לר"י: כיון דס"ד דליכא תיקון כלל במתני', א"כ תקשי לכ"ע: היכי חייב לר"ש מקלקל בחבורה? הא מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה היא, ופטור אפילו בחבורה! כדמוכח בסוף כל כתבי (שבת קכא:), דפטר ר"ש התם הורג נחשים ועקרבים משום מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה; ובריש הנחנקין (סנהדרין פד:) נמי מסיק: "מאן שמעת ליה דאמר מקלקל בחבורה חייב? ר"ש, האמר מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה פטור עליה":
Tosafot on Pesachim 73a:4:1.english: "According to the one who says that one who acts destructively in [inflicting] a wound, etc." - And if you ask: Is it not R' Yehudah who exempts one who acts destructively in [inflicting] a wound, whereas our Mishnah, which holds [the slaughterer] liable in [the case of] those who are unfit [to eat it] — which is [a case of] one who acts preoccupiedly (mit'asek), who slaughters this sacrifice thinking it is another [one] — does not follow R' Yehudah, since according to him one who acts preoccupiedly is exempt? As is proven in the chapter Safek Akhal (Keritot 19b), where it states: "Leave aside [the case of] infants; since one who acts destructively in [inflicting] a wound is liable, one who acts preoccupiedly is also liable." Thus it implies that the one who exempts one who acts destructively in [inflicting] a wound also exempts one who acts preoccupiedly; and if so, our Mishnah cannot be established according to the one who exempts one who acts destructively in [inflicting] a wound! And one can answer: [The statement] "According to the one who says that one who acts destructively in [inflicting] a wound is exempt" refers to R' Yochanan according to R' Shimon, who exempts where one acts completely destructively, such that there is no constructive improvement at all — and to exclude [the view of] R' Abbahu. For in the chapter HaOreg (Shabbat 106a), R' Abbahu taught before R' Yochanan: "All who act destructively are exempt, except for one who inflicts a wound and one who kindles a fire." He [R' Yochanan] said to him: "Go out and teach [this] outside; 'one who inflicts a wound and one who kindles a fire' is not [an authoritative] baraita! And even if you say it is [an authoritative] baraita, [it speaks] of one who inflicts a wound and needs [the blood] for his dog, and one who kindles a fire and needs its ash." And this is according to R' Shimon, since he distinguishes between one who inflicts a wound and one who kindles a fire and other destructive acts; however, [for] one who acts completely destructively, [he is] not [liable], even according to R' Shimon. However, it is still difficult to R' Yitzchak (Ri): Since it is currently assumed that there is no constructive improvement at all in our Mishnah, if so, it should be difficult according to everyone: how is one who acts destructively in [inflicting] a wound liable according to R' Shimon? Why, it is a labor not needed for its own sake (melakhah she'einah tzerikhah legufah), and he is exempt even in [inflicting] a wound! As is proven at the end of Kol Kitvei (Shabbat 121b), where R' Shimon exempts there one who kills snakes and scorpions because of [it being] a labor not needed for its own sake; and at the beginning of HaNeḥnakin (Sanhedrin 84b) as well, [the Gemara] concludes: "Whom have you heard say that one who acts destructively in [inflicting] a wound is liable? R' Shimon — [yet] he has said that for a labor not needed for its own sake one is exempt!"

Tosafot on Pesachim 73a:7:1.hebrew: שחטו ונמצא טריפה בסתר פטור - תימה לר"י: אמאי פטור? והלא לא עשה מצוה! ומתניתין אוקימנא כר"ש, דמחייב אפי' לר' יהושע היכא דלא עשה מצוה. וליכא למימר דהכא פטור משום דחשבי' ליה כאנוס, דע"כ לאו מטעם אנוס פטר ליה, אלא משום דטעה בדבר מצוה — כדמוכח בגמ', דפריך: אי ר' אליעזר, חטאת נמי מחייב, דהא לית ליה טעה בדבר מצוה פטור. ותי' ר"י דכל זה מדברי ר"מ:
Tosafot on Pesachim 73a:7:1.english: "He slaughtered it and it was found to be a tereifah in a hidden [part], he is exempt" - This is astonishing to Ri: why is he exempt? Did he not fail to perform a mitzvah? And we established our Mishnah in accordance with R. Shimon, who holds [one] liable even according to R. Yehoshua where he did not perform a mitzvah! And one cannot say that here he is exempt because we consider him as one acting under duress [anus], for perforce it is not on the grounds of duress that [the Tanna] exempts him, but rather because he erred in a matter of a mitzvah — as is proven in the Gemara, which asks: "If [it is] R. Eliezer, he should also be liable for a sin-offering, for he does not hold [that] one who erred in a matter of a mitzvah is exempt." And Ri answered that all of this is from the words of R. Meir.

Tosafot on Pesachim 73a:9:1.hebrew: תיקן להוציאו מידי אבר מן החי - משמע דתקרובת ע"ז מטמאה מדאורייתא, מדלא קאמר "תיקן להוציאו מידי נבילה", ולא מיחייב אהך טומאה אם נכנס למקדש. ובע"ז פ' ר' ישמעאל (עבודה זרה דף נב.) משמע שהיא מדרבנן, דבעי רבי יוחנן: "תקרובת ע"ז של אוכלין מהו כו', או דילמא איסורא דאורייתא לא בטלה, טומאה דרבנן בטלה". וי"ל דאיצטריך הכא לשנויי "תיקן להוציאו מאמה"ח", כי היכי דלא ניפשוט מהך ברייתא דטומאת תקרובת לאו דאורייתא. וכן בסוף העור והרוטב (חולין קכט.), דאמר אביי: "הרי אמרו תקרובת ע"ז של אוכלין מטמא — טומאתה לאו דאורייתא, דאי דאורייתא מצינו לאוכלין שמטמא טומאה חמורה", ומשני: "כששימש מעשה עץ שימש" — התם נמי דיחויה בעלמא הוא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 73a:9:1.english: He improved [it] by removing it from [the category of] a limb from a living creature - This implies that an offering to idolatry imparts ritual impurity by Torah law, since [the Gemara] does not say "he improved [it] by removing it from [the category of] a carcass (neveilah)," so that he would not be liable for that impurity if he enters the Temple. And in Avodah Zarah, chapter Rabbi Yishmael (Avodah Zarah 52a), it implies that it is rabbinic, as Rabbi Yochanan asks: "What is [the law regarding] an idolatrous offering of foodstuffs, etc., or perhaps a biblical prohibition is not nullified, [whereas] a rabbinic impurity is nullified?" And one can answer that here it was necessary to answer "he improved [it] by removing it from [the category of] a limb from a living creature" so that we would not resolve from this baraita that the impurity of an offering [to idolatry] is not biblical. And similarly at the end of [chapter] HaOr VeHaRotev (Chullin 129a), where Abaye says: "Behold, they said [that] an idolatrous offering of foodstuffs imparts impurity — its impurity is not biblical, for if it were biblical, we would have found foodstuffs that impart severe impurity," and [the Gemara] answers: "When it served [the idol], it served as an act of wood" — there too, it is merely a deflection.
